copy.bis: Kay walay tagtugnaw sa Pilipinas, aktibo ang mga insekto sa tibuok tuig — mao nga mas dako ang tsansa nga modaghan sila kumpara sa bugnaw nga nasod, diin daghan ang mamatay o matulog sa tagtugnaw.

copy.tl: Sa gabi, humuhuli ng lamok at gamu-gamo ang mga panikin na kumakain ng insekto.
copy.bis: Sa gabii, modakop og namok ug anunugba ang mga kabog nga mokaon ug insekto.

assignedReviews.reason: Side breathing holes are not head, legs or wings used to move and gather food.

copy.en:
How does an insect breathe?

An insect doesn't breathe through a nose — it breathes through tiny holes along the sides of its body!
copy.tl:
Paano humihinga ang insekto?

Hindi sa ilong humihinga ang insekto — humihinga ito sa maliliit na butas sa gilid ng katawan nito!
copy.bis:
Giunsa pag-ginhawa sa insekto?

Dili sa ilong moginhawa ang insekto — moginhawa kini pinaagi sa gagmay nga mga lungag sa kilid sa lawas niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An insect's eyes sit on its head, and each one is made up of many, many tiny parts.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (eyes on the head) but does not identify the role of eyes in moving or gathering food, which is the core action of the competency. It only provides structural information about insect eyes.

copy.en: An insect's eyes sit on its head, and each one is made up of many, many tiny parts.
copy.tl: Ang mata ng insekto ay nasa ulo nito, at binubuo ito ng maraming maliliit na bahagi.
copy.bis: Ang mata sa insekto anaa sa ulo niini, ug gilangkuban kini og daghang gagmay nga bahin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because their lenses curve all around, many insects can see almost every direction at once
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food

copy.en:
How do insects see in all directions?

Because their lenses curve all around, many insects can see almost every direction at once — no need to turn their head!
copy.tl:
Paano nakakakita ang insekto sa lahat ng direksyon?

Dahil paikot ang ayos ng kanilang mga lente, maraming insekto ay halos nakakakita sa lahat ng direksyon nang sabay-sabay — hindi na kailangang lumingon!
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagkakita sa insekto sa tanang direksyon?

Tungod kay nakakurba ang pagkahan-ay sa ilang mga lente, daghang insekto makakita sa halos tanang direksyon dungan — dili na kinahanglan mosimang!

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a survival strategy (overwintering as eggs or larvae), which is an adaptation to cold, but it does not describe how animals have changed to better suit their environment through mimicry, camouflage, or other evolutionary changes. It only states a behavioral/life-history response, not a change suited to the environment.

copy.en: Many insects survive cold weather as eggs or larvae, staying in a deep resting state until warmth returns.
copy.tl: Maraming insekto ang nakakaligtas sa malamig na panahon bilang itlog o uod na nasa malalim na pahinga hanggang bumalik ang init.
copy.bis: Daghang insekto ang mabuhi sa bugnaw nga panahon isip itlog o ulod nga anaa sa lawom nga pahulay hangtod mobalik ang kainit.

assignedReviews.reason: The card only identifies the seismograph as the instrument that detects and records earthquakes. The competency requires making models of fault scenarios to illustrate epicenter, intensity, and tsunamis, which the card does not support.

copy.en: Feel the shake! A seismograph is the instrument that detects and records earthquakes.
copy.tl: Ramdam ang yanig! Ang seismograph ang instrumentong sumusukat at nagtatala ng lindol.
copy.bis: Bati ang linog! Ang seismograph ang instrumento nga mosukod ug morekord sa linog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mosquitoes undergo internal fertilization, as the male's reproductive organ extends into the female's body to deposit sperm.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: their fertilization is internal

copy.en: Mosquitoes undergo internal fertilization, as the male's reproductive organ extends into the female's body to deposit sperm.
copy.tl: Ang mga lamok ay sumasailalim sa internal fertilization, dahil ang reproductive organ ng lalaki ay pumapasok sa katawan ng babae para magdeposito ng sperm.
copy.bis: Ang mga lamok moagi sa internal fertilization, tungod kay ang reproductive organ sa laki mosulod sa lawas sa baye aron magdeposito ug sperm.

copy.en: Every website you open is stored on a powerful, always-on computer called a server! When you click a link, your phone simply asks that server for the information.
copy.tl: Ang bawat website na binubuksan mo ay naka-store sa isang makapangyarihang computer na laging bukas na tinatawag na server! Kapag nag-click ka, hinihingi ng telepono mo ang impormasyon mula sa server na iyon.
copy.bis: Ang matag website nga imong ablihan gitipigan sa usa ka kusgan nga computer nga kanunay naka-on nga gitawag ug server! Ug kung mo-click ka, ang imong telepono mangayo ug impormasyon gikan niana nga server.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The medicine weakens or kills the worms inside your intestine. They let go of their grip and pass out with your poop
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and labeled diagrams the parts of the digestive system as mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine, and describe how they work

copy.en:
How does deworming medicine work?

The medicine weakens or kills the worms inside your intestine. They let go of their grip and pass out with your poop — bye-bye worms!
copy.tl:
Paano gumagana ang gamot sa bulati?

Pinapahina o pinapatay ng gamot ang mga bulati sa loob ng bituka mo. Binibitawan nila ang kapit nila at lumalabas kasama ng tae — paalam, bulati!
copy.bis:
Unsaon paglihok sa tambal sa bulati?

Ang tambal mopaluya o mopatay sa bulati sulod sa imong tinai. Buhian nila ang ilang kupot ug mogawas uban sa imong tae — babay, bulati!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Both are intestinal worms, but a roundworm is big and long like an earthworm, while a pinworm is tiny
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a roundworm is big and long like an earthworm, while a pinworm is tiny, thin, and white
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: Two worm sizes are not the difference between animals with a backbone and animals without backbones.

copy.en:
How are roundworms and pinworms different?

Both are intestinal worms, but a roundworm is big and long like an earthworm, while a pinworm is tiny, thin, and white like a little thread!
copy.tl:
Paano magkaiba ang roundworm at pinworm?

Pareho silang bulati sa loob ng tiyan, pero malaki at mahaba ang roundworm na parang earthworm, samantalang ang pinworm ay napakaliit, manipis, at puti tulad ng hibla ng sinulid!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkalahi ang roundworm ug pinworm?

Pareho silang bulati sa lawas, apan dako ug taas ang roundworm murag earthworm, samtang ang pinworm gamay kaayo, nipis, ug puti sama sa hilo!

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a specific micronutrient (iodine) deficiency and its effects on growth and learning, but does not teach the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter) as required by G3-L-6. It is only tangentially related to food/nutrition.

copy.en: Long-term iodine deficiency in children can slow down their growth and learning.
copy.tl: Ang matagal na kakulangan sa iodine sa mga bata ay maaaring magpabagal ng kanilang paglaki at pag-aaral.
copy.bis: Ang dugay nga kakulangan sa iodine sa mga bata makapahinay sa ilang pagtubo ug pagkat-on.

The content is in the same matter domain but provides no instructional support for this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: share one electron pair so both reach 8
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the indicators for a chemical reaction as color change, the formation of a precipitate, the release of gas, and or odor, or a change in temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how iodine and chlorine share electrons to form a molecule. It does not describe any indicator of a chemical reaction (color change, precipitate, gas, odor, or temperature change). The topic is chemical bonding, not reaction indicators, so it only shares the broad chemistry subject.

copy.en: Iodine monochloride forms when one iodine atom and one chlorine atom, each with 7 valence electrons, share one electron pair so both reach 8.
copy.tl: Nabubuo ang iodine monochloride kapag ang isang iodine atom at isang chlorine atom, na parehong may 7 valence electrons, ay nagbahagi ng isang electron pair para pareho silang umabot sa 8.
copy.bis: Ang iodine monochloride maporma kon ang usa ka iodine atom ug usa ka chlorine atom, nga ang matag usa adunay 7 ka valence electrons, mipaambit og usa ka electron pair aron ang duha makaabot sa 8.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it tells the thyroid when to work and how much hormone to make
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes hormonal control between the pituitary and thyroid, but does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations, and does not explain how body systems work together such as digestion and excretion. It is only loosely related to organ-system coordination.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it tells the thyroid when to work and how much hormone to make
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions regulation of hormone production, which is a homeostatic-type control, but it does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems or address indicators such as body temperature, glucose level, or blood pressure. It provides no direct instructional support for this competency.

copy.en:
Who tells the thyroid when to work?

A small brain part called the pituitary gland acts like the boss — it tells the thyroid when to work and how much hormone to make.
copy.tl:
Sino ang bumabantay sa thyroid?

May maliit na bahagi ng utak na tinatawag na pituitary gland na parang boss — ito ang nag-uutos sa thyroid kung kailan magtrabaho at gaano karaming hormone ang gagawin.
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang nagbantay sa thyroid?

Adunay gamay nga bahin sa utok nga gitawag og pituitary gland nga sama sa boss — kini ang nagsugo sa thyroid kung kanus-a motrabaho ug pila ka hormone ang himoon.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions iodized salt, which is a mixture, but it does not describe uniform vs non-uniform mixtures, solutions, or suspensions. It only states that iodine is added by law to prevent goiter, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Iodized salt has iodine added by law to prevent iodine deficiency disorders like goiter. In the Philippines, salt iodization is required under the ASIN Law!
copy.tl: Ang iodized salt ay may iodine na idinagdag ng batas para iwasan ang mga sakit tulad ng goiter. Sa Pilipinas, sapwat ito sa ilalim ng ASIN Law!
copy.bis: Ang iodized salt adunay iodine nga gidugang sa balaod aron mapugngan ang mga sakit sama sa goiter. Sa Pilipinas, gikinahanglan kini sa ASIN Law!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: fertilizers that are often ionic compounds

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions ionic compounds and nutrients (potassium, nitrate) but does not teach writing chemical formulas or names of specific ionic compounds such as NaCl, MgO, KCl, or MgCl2. It only provides a general context about ionic fertilizers.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: help them grow big and strong

copy.en: Filipino farmers use fertilizers that are often ionic compounds. These give plants nutrients like potassium and nitrate to help them grow big and strong!
copy.tl: Gumagamit ang mga magsasaka sa Pilipinas ng pataba na madalas ay ionic compounds. Nagbibigay ito ng nutrients gaya ng potassium at nitrate para lumago ang mga halaman!
copy.bis: Gigamit sa mga mag-uuma sa Pilipinas ang abono nga kasagaran ionic compounds. Naghatag kini og nutrients sama sa potassium ug nitrate aron motubo ang mga tanom!

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses iron as a nutrient and its potential harm, but does not teach the basic needs of living things such as air, food, water, and shelter. It only tangentially relates to food/nutrition.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions liver and organ damage but does not describe how any human body system works (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory). It is about iron toxicity, not system function.

copy.en: The body needs iron, but too much can be harmful—high doses, especially from supplements without a doctor's advice, can damage the liver and other organs.
copy.tl: Kailangan ng katawan ang iron, pero ang sobra ay puwede ring makasama—lalo na ang supplement na ininom nang walang payo ng doktor, na puwedeng makapinsala sa atay.
copy.bis: Gikinahanglan sa lawas ang iron, apan ang sobra makadaot usab—ilabina ang supplement nga giinom nga walay tambag sa doktor, nga makadaot sa atay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: iron, which your body needs to make healthy red blood cells
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions red blood cells, which belong to the circulatory system, but it does not describe how the circulatory system works. It only states a nutritional fact about iron and red blood cell production, providing no direct instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter

copy.en: Leafy greens like malunggay and kangkong are packed with iron, which your body needs to make healthy red blood cells.
copy.tl: Ang mga madahong gulay tulad ng malunggay at kangkong ay mayaman sa iron, na kailangan ng katawan para makagawa ng malusog na pulang selula ng dugo.
copy.bis: Ang mga dahonon nga utanon sama sa malunggay ug kangkong dato sa iron, nga gikinahanglan sa lawas aron makahimo og himsog nga pula nga selula sa dugo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When a little carbon is mixed with iron, it becomes steel
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions mixing carbon with iron to form steel, which is technically a mixture (alloy), but it does not describe it as a uniform or non-uniform mixture, nor does it relate to solutions or suspensions as required by the competency. It only provides a fact about steel formation without teaching the classification of mixtures.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it becomes steel, which is harder and stronger

assignedReviews.reason: The competency focuses on how changes in solid materials (shaping, pressing, hammering, joining, cutting) make them useful. The connection is only that a change makes a material useful, which is too broad.

copy.en:
How do we make iron even stronger?

When a little carbon is mixed with iron, it becomes steel, which is harder and stronger!
copy.tl:
Paano natin ginagawang mas matibay ang iron?

Kapag hinaluan ng kaunting carbon ang iron, nagiging asero ito na mas matigas at matibay!
copy.bis:
Unsaon paghimo sa puthaw nga mas lig-on?

Kon sagolan og gamay nga karbon ang puthaw, mahimo kining asero nga mas gahi ug lig-on!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: more area can support more kinds of animals and plants and more varied habitats
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss the factors that limit the ecosystem's carrying capacity, such as adequate food, shelter, water, and mates
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains species richness on islands via area and habitat variety, but does not discuss limiting factors of carrying capacity such as food, shelter, water, or mates. It is only tangentially related to ecosystem carrying capacity.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: more area can support more kinds of animals and plants and more varied habitats
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the advantage of high biodiversity in maintaining the stability of an ecosystem during difficult conditions, such as food shortages, disease, and climate change
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions more species and varied habitats, but does not explain how high biodiversity maintains ecosystem stability during difficult conditions like food shortages, disease, or climate change. It does not directly support the competency's core concept.

copy.en:
Why do bigger islands have more species?

Bigger islands usually have more species than small ones, because more area can support more kinds of animals and plants and more varied habitats.
copy.tl:
Bakit mas maraming species ang malaking pulo?

Karaniwang mas maraming species ang malalaking pulo kaysa sa maliliit, dahil mas malaking lugar ang nagbibigay-suporta sa mas maraming species at iba't ibang tirahan.
copy.bis:
Nganong mas daghang species ang dako nga pulo?

Kasagarang mas daghang species ang dagko nga pulo kay sa gagmay, kay ang mas dako nga lugar makasuporta og mas daghang species ug lain-laing puy-anan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You can't pour water into a cup in space!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card illustrates that gravity affects water behavior, but the competency specifically addresses gravity's effects on Earth. The card is set in space (microgravity), so it does not directly support the Earth-focused competency.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water (a liquid) but does not describe shape or volume properties of solids, liquids, or gases. It only implies that water does not pour in space, which is not about definite/indefinite shape or volume.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You can't pour water into a cup in space!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the effects of gravity to the motion of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows an effect of gravity (water not pouring), but it does not describe the motion of an object under gravity. It is about a liquid's behavior in microgravity, not the motion of an object.

copy.en: You can't pour water into a cup in space! Instead, astronauts drink through a straw from a sealed pouch.
copy.tl: Hindi pwedeng magbuhos ng tubig sa baso sa kalawakan! Kaya umiinom ang mga astronaut gamit ang straw mula sa selyadong supot.
copy.bis: Dili pwede magbubo og tubig sa baso sa kawanangan! Mao nga moinom ang mga astronaut gamit ang straw gikan sa selyadong supot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It was built by 15 countries, including the United States, Russia, Japan, Canada, and European Space Agency members!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how modern research about celestial objects uses new space technologies including telescopes and space probes
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes who built the ISS, a space station, but does not explain how modern research about celestial objects uses telescopes or space probes. The ISS is not a telescope or space probe, and the card does not address research on celestial objects. It is only tangentially related to space technology.

copy.en:
Who built the International Space Station (ISS) in space?

What's the biggest spider by leg span?

By leg span, the giant huntsman spider from Laos is the biggest, spreading its legs up to about 30 cm.
copy.tl:
Alin ang pinakamalaking gagamba sa buong mundo?

Kung sukat ng binti ang basehan, ang giant huntsman spider mula sa Laos ang pinakamalaki, na umaabot ng mga 30 cm ang lapad.
copy.bis:
Hain ang pinakadako nga lawalawa sa tibuok kalibutan?

Kon ang gilapdon sa tiil ang basihan, ang giant huntsman spider gikan sa Laos mao ang pinakadako, nga mokabat og mga 30 cm.

assignedReviews.reason: The card only states a wingspan measurement for the wandering albatross. It does not describe the outer body part (wings) or identify their role in movement or gathering food, which is the focus of G3-L-4.

copy.en:
Which bird has the biggest wingspan?

The wandering albatross wins — its wingspan is almost 3 meters from tip to tip, the largest of any bird!
copy.tl:
Aling ibon may pinakamalapad na pakpak?

Ang wandering albatross ang panalo — halos 3 metro ang pakpak nito mula dulo hanggang dulo, ang pinakamalapad sa lahat ng ibon!
copy.bis:
Unsa nga langgam ang adunay pinakalapad nga pako?

Ang wandering albatross ang midaog — halos 3 ka metro ang pako niini gikan sa tumoy ngadto sa tumoy, ang pinakalapad sa tanang langgam!

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a type of soil and mentions metal ores, but it does not explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals. It only gives a characteristic of laterite, not the formation process.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Laterite is a red, crumbly tropical soil
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities using simple equipment to compare different types of soil including sandy, clay, silt, and loam, including comparing the ability of the soils to hold water
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions one soil type (laterite) but does not compare sandy, clay, silt, and loam soils or their water-holding ability, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Laterite is a red, crumbly tropical soil found in hot, humid places like the Philippines! Heavy rain washes away plant nutrients but leaves behind rich metal ores like nickel.
copy.tl: Ang laterite ay mapula at madurog na tropical na lupa sa mainit na lugar tulad ng Pilipinas! Hinuhugasan ng ulan ang sustansya ng halaman, pero nag-iiwan ng maraming metal ore tulad ng nickel.
copy.bis: Ang laterite usa ka pula ug madurog nga tropical nga yuta sa mainit nga lugar sama sa Pilipinas! Ang kusog nga ulan nagtangtang sa sustansya sa tanom, pero nagbilin og daghang metal ore sama sa nickel.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies Lavoisier as a famous foreign scientist but does not mention any invention or specific contribution, which is a required part of the competency. It only provides a title, not the scientist's invention/s.

copy.en:
Who is called the "Father of Modern Chemistry"?

Antoine Lavoisier is called the "Father of Modern Chemistry"!
copy.tl:
Sino ang tinaguriang "Ama ng Modernong Kimika"?

Si Antoine Lavoisier ang tinaguriang "Ama ng Modernong Kimika"!
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang gitawag nga "Amahan sa Modernong Chemistry"?

Si Antoine Lavoisier ang gitawag nga "Amahan sa Modernong Chemistry"!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the angle of reflection always equals the angle of incidence
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card states the law of reflection (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection), which is foundational knowledge for describing reflection. However, the competency requires carrying out guided investigations to describe and illustrate reflection using plane and curved mirrors, and refraction using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with everyday examples. The card does not address mirrors, refraction, investigations, or everyday applications, so it only provides background knowledge rather than directly supporting the stated skill.

copy.en: When light reflects off a surface, the angle of reflection always equals the angle of incidence — this is the law of reflection!
copy.tl: Kapag ang liwanag ay sumasalamin sa isang ibabaw, ang angle of reflection ay palaging katumbas ng angle of incidence — ito ang law of reflection!
copy.bis: Kung ang suga mobunal sa ibabaw, ang angle of reflection kanunay katumbas sa angle of incidence — kini ang law of reflection!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The alternator converts engine energy back into stored chemical energy to recharge them.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify examples of everyday situations that demonstrate: a. kinetic energy being transformed to potential energy, and b. potential energy being transformed to kinetic energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes conversion of engine (mechanical) energy into chemical energy for recharging a lead-acid battery. It does not address kinetic energy transforming to potential energy or potential energy transforming to kinetic energy, which is the specific skill of G8-F-5. The topic is energy transformation but not the required kinetic/potential pair.

copy.en:
What makes a car battery special and rechargeable?

Car batteries are lead-acid batteries with lead plates and sulfuric acid electrolyte! The alternator converts engine energy back into stored chemical energy to recharge them.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nagpapatibay at nagpaparecharge sa baterya ng sasakyan?

Ang mga baterya ng sasakyan ay lead-acid batteries na may lead plates at sulfuric acid electrolyte! Ang alternator ay nagko-convert ng engine energy pabalik sa chemical energy para mag-recharge.
copy.bis:
Unsay naghimo sa baterya sa sasakyan nga espesyal ug ma-recharge?

Ang mga baterya sa sasakyan mga lead-acid battery nga adunay lead plates ug sulfuric acid electrolyte! Ang alternator nagconvert sa engine energy balik ngadto sa chemical energy aron mag-recharge.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: look for the leaf that moves on its own
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a leaf insect's camouflage-like appearance but does not describe how the animal has changed to suit its environment, nor does it involve using information from secondary sources as required by the competency.

copy.en:
How do you spot a hidden leaf insect?

To spot a hidden leaf insect, don't look for the bug — look for the leaf that moves on its own. That's usually where it's hiding!
copy.tl:
Paano makikita ang nagtatagong leaf insect?

Kung gusto mong makahanap ng leaf insect, huwag hanapin ang insekto — hanapin ang dahong gumagalaw nang mag-isa. Doon mo ito madalas matutuklasan!
copy.bis:
Unsaon makit-an ang nagtago nga leaf insect?

Kon gusto nimong makakita og leaf insect, ayaw pangitaa ang insekto — pangitaa ang dahon nga molihok nga mag-isa. Didto kasagaran nimo kini makita!
